correctness.rationale: With the empty subsequence included, the shifted ending counts start at (1,1), undergo the two determinant-one shears, and output x+y−1. Positive coprime lifts exist for every primitive vector by CRT avoidance of the finitely many prime divisors of the chosen second lift; subtractive Euclid gives all reachable vectors and, with word order reversed, all primitive suffix rows. In a basis beginning with v, rows taking values (1,0) and (1,1) distinguish v from any unequal w for the residue-0 predicate. For the residue-−1 predicate the primitive annihilator (−v₂,v₁) identifies exactly the unit multiples of v; freeness and the prime-power counts give the stated projective count for composite as well as prime m. Pure-letter suffixes of length m−1 recover each coordinate of a Moore state separately. This covers m=2, the empty input, and complete machines. A separate bounded check minimized all three machines for m=2 through 8 and compared prefix outputs against explicit subsequence sets through word length 6; it is corroboration, not the all-m proof.
residual_risks: No formal proof certificate is claimed; the bounded replay does not replace the ring argument.
